LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to use correct tenses in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences
2. use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses
3. appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 VERBS AND TENSE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses

What this means
In this part you learn to use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a partner. (skill: use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences.
3. Practise this skill: use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the correct use of verbs and tenses for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to use correct tenses in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar In Use 3.3.1 Verbs and Tense means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify regular and irregular verbs in sentences.
5. Be able to: use regular and irregular verbs to construct sentences using the past, present, and future tenses.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
